title: Annotatio VI §.VIII: convert conditional to absolute — Reformati do believe substantial presence
pass_a_gloss: And let them convert this Conditional Proposition of theirs — If the Reformed truly believed what they pretend to believe, namely that Christ’s Body and blood are truly and Substantially present in the Holy Supper, not only would much of the Controversy’s moment depart, but also the way would be fortified to composing more easily the remaining heads — into this absolute and categorical one, which even Christian charity, by nearly all its essential attributes described by the Apostle in 1 Cor. 13, demands of them: The Reformed beyond doubt believe what they say they believe, namely that Christ’s body and blood are truly and substantially present in the Sacred Supper — and so not only is every moment of Controversy wanting, but also the way is fortified to composing more easily the fewer and lesser remaining heads among Evangelicals.
pass_b_english: Convert their conditional — “if the Reformed really believed substantial presence, controversy would shrink and the rest would compose easier” — into the absolute charity demands (1 Cor 13).
The Reformed beyond doubt believe what they say: body and blood truly and substantially present — so the main moment of controversy is gone, and the way to lesser remaining heads is open.
source_text: Et Propositionem hanc suam Conditionatam: Si reverà hoc crederent, quod se credere simulant Reformati, nempe Corpus & sanguinem Christi, verè & Substantialiter adesse in S. Cœna, non modo plurimum decessurum esse momento Controversiæ, sed & munitum iri aditum ad ea quæ restant capita facilius componenda, in hanc absolutam & categoricam convertant, quam vel charitas Christiana, per omnia propemodum attributa sua essentialia, Apostolo 1. Cor. XIII. descripta, ab iis efflagitat: Reformati credunt proculdubio, quod credere se dicunt, nempe corpus & sanguinem Christi verè & substantialiter adesse in Sacra Cœna, sicque non modo deest omne momentum Controversiæ, sed & munitus aditus ad ea quæ restant pauciora minoraque inter Evangelicos capita facilius componenda.
